body:
**Nonauthor source review of the verification museum at exact head `cd32303bcf0fe4a91a1a1f2aad2b5b6eb45088d6` (merged as `d77a85a7`): delivered. Pickup [5848647694](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/main/pull/151#issuecomment-5848647694) is RELEASED by this comment.**

Disclosure: Anthropic Claude, Claude Code cloud session `session_01Cz7WZybv8znP64SpPj6sWY`, source-exposed, same GitHub account and owner as the author lane: **zero organizational-independence credit**; any gate that requires independence stays open. The offer ([5848315997](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/main/pull/151#issuecomment-5848315997)) and the PR body are OpenAI-origin text that I read. Scientific effect **NONE**: this is a review of display and guard interfaces; it tests, supports or weakens no mathematical claim, and no status label moves.

Timing: picked up 2026-09-26, delivered 2026-10-13. The delay is this session's (other lanes, two outages), not the author's. The reviewed head is a merged commit and did not change, so the binding stands.

### 1. Inputs and baseline

- The `cd32303` tree was extracted to a read-only directory; its 104 tracked files are byte-identical to `git show cd32303:<path>` (re-checked independently by each second reader). Current main is a successor and is not under review; see §7 for the few validation-only re-probes against it.
- **The 19 SHA-256 identities of the PR body: 19 of 19 hold at `cd32303`; 0 of 19 hold on current `main` `f6911c25`** (all nineteen files have changed since 26 September).
- Offline fixtures: all 30 `SOURCES` pins were rebuilt from git objects (Math-@`d6628da`, main@`71400b94`) and from the `PROOF_INDEX.md` bytes embedded in `cd32303`'s own `tests/test_museum_data.py` (12,708 B, blob `e4cb1d94`, sha256 `f9c4db77…`), each accepted only after `cd32303`'s `museum_data.verify_bytes` (byte count, git blob SHA-1, SHA-256). `README.md@d6628da` was not available in one harness, so its D2/D4/D6 cards refuse there with a 404 and those end-to-end renders use the other cards. No probe used the network; Q4-5 uses a local socketpair.
- **Baseline, the shipped page is right.** The committed `museum.json` passes `validateBoundManifest` against the real index and STATUS bytes and renders 14 cards. All fourteen shipped proof and review bindings are correct: no review equals its proof, each review fills the review role of its bullet, each byte-verified review sits at the index commit, and each of the seven byte-verified reviews records ACCEPT at its stated scope. The three AMEND rows render as AMEND/open with "OPEN / NOT LANDED". **Every finding below is a guard or interface defect (what would not be refused), not wrong data on the page.**
- Mutant notation: S1–S4 are the four CI commands of `.github/workflows/public-shop.yml` run offline on a scratch copy of the tree (S1 `unittest … test_museum_data.py`; S2 `tools/museum_check.py --math-root <verified fixture>`; S3 `node --test tests/test_museum_geometry.mjs`; S4 `node --test tests/test_public_shop_frontend.mjs`). "Survived" means all four stayed green with that guard deleted. Killed controls (M11 pointer-source identity, M17 replay-source verification, M24 proof-byte verification, M28 status authority, G01 geometry identity, P02 review-pointer binding, P11 `check_export`) show the harness does detect what the tests cover.

### 2. Coverage: read this before the findings

- **Two adversarial second reads** (independent re-reproduction at the `cd32303` bytes, refute-by-default; all reproduced, none refuted): **Q1-1 to Q1-9, Q2-F1 to Q2-F6, Q3-F1, Q3-F2** (17 findings).
- **Single-reader** (this session only): **Q3-F3 to Q3-F5, Q4-1 to Q4-7, FO-1 to FO-8** (18 findings). Their probes were re-run tonight in an isolated environment with output matching the recorded observations, and I re-read every cited line myself, but no second reader has seen them: this session's parallel-review capacity is exhausted until 2026-10-17 03:00Z. Treat them as one reader's claims with reproducing probes.
- Severity is the finder's; where a second reader rated differently, both are shown. Tally: 3 critical, 12 important, 20 minor. Line numbers are at `cd32303`.

### 3. Findings

**Q1 — cross-claim proof/review substitution**

**Q1-1 [critical; 2 reads, one rates important] A claim's own proof, or any other link in its bullet or row, is accepted as its "Byte-verified review".** `tools/museum_data.py:401-406` binds a review only by `"](" + review_path + ")"` occurring somewhere in the claim's own PROOF_INDEX bullet, and every bullet also links the claim's proof; `docs/site/museum.mjs:51-53, 86` (`sourceContainsPath`, including the `/${path})` suffix clause) accept any link in the quote, and any path that is a suffix of one. Probes `substitution/p1_review_role.{py,mjs}`, `p1b_suffix_match.mjs`: review := own proof on d5-two-scale and D2 is accepted by `project()`, by `museum_check` (regenerates the same bytes) and by `validateBoundManifest`; the card shows "Byte-verified review" with the review link equal to the proof link. The D5 AMEND row's mutable `blob/main/PROOF_INDEX.md` link lets the pinned index itself pass as that card's "Byte-verified review" next to "Unmerged review pointer only"; `claims/LANDING_CLAIMS.json` passes as the P15 card's review. Control: a review not in the bullet is refused. The one negative control (`test_misdirected_review_pointer_refused`) does not cover this. Fix: require the review to be the link in the review role of the bullet and to differ from the proof; match exact link targets, not suffixes; bind the D5 open review outside the pointer branch too. The second reader who rated it important did so because the only path to the bad display is a maintainer error in the hard-coded spec table or a hand-edited manifest served without CI, while class, source label, "OPEN / NOT LANDED" and the verbatim quote stay bound independently.

**Q1-2 [important; 2 reads] A byte-verified review's repository and commit are not bound to the index snapshot.** `museum.mjs:75` binds the proof to `index_source.repository/commit`; `:86` checks a non-pointer review by path only; `museum_data.py:405-406` takes whatever `SOURCES[path]` pins. Probe `substitution/p2_review_snapshot.{py,mjs}`: the same review path at Math-@`11111111…` or in `query-`@`22222222…` is accepted and rendered "Byte-verified review" with that other identity, with a synthetic AMEND verdict shown under an ACCEPT-scoped card; the same change on the proof is refused. Fix: apply the proof rule to reviews.

**Q1-3 [important; 2 reads] Pointer binding is an undelimited substring test; a non-boolean `pointer_only` skips the URL and notice checks.** `museum.mjs:85` `pointerText.includes(review_url)` vs the builder's delimited `"](url)"` (`museum_data.py:404`); `:40` enforces the URL shape and notice only for `pointer_only===true` while `:82, :151-154` branch on truthiness. Probe `substitution/p3_pointer_substring.mjs`: `main/issues/6` passes on D3 (bullet links #65), `main/issues/7` on D4 (#76), a truncated comment id passes, and `{pointer_only:1, review_url:""}` turns d5-two-scale's byte-verified review into "Review pointer in the verified index" linking PROOF_INDEX.md with no not-byte-frozen notice. Fix: delimited match as in the builder; `=== true` everywhere. (Overlaps Q2-F2, FO-2; reported once each from their lens.)

**Q1-4 [important; 2 reads] The remote, annulus and p15 exhibits are titled after the D4/D5/D6 claims but not bound to those claims' proofs; only `lifetime` is.** `museum.mjs:100-101` (`sameIdentity` for lifetime alone), `:197-203` (quote checked against the exhibit's own bytes), `geometry.mjs:386-391` (repository and path, not commit or digest). Probe `substitution/p4_exhibit_binding.mjs`: `exhibits.annulus` repinned to commit `44444444…` with a synthetic widened statement renders under the D5 title with geometry mounted and the widened text as "Exact source excerpt"; the same change on `lifetime` is refused; `exhibits.remote := D5 height-window proof` passes `validateBoundManifest` (geometry refuses it only after the card is appended). Second reader extended it to `remote` and `p15`. Fix: bind each exhibit to its claim's proof identity.

**Q1-5 [important; 2 reads] A replay command is not bound to its claim: with the shared Math- README as source, any README command passes for any claim.** `museum_data.py:263-341, 410-418` (commands hard-coded, never compared with text); `museum.mjs:96-98, 118` (command must be some line of the replay source). Probe `substitution/p5_replay_binding.{py,mjs}`: D2↔D6 swapped, D4 given the D0 `hard_gate.py` command, the engineering-only P15 counterexample given the D6 `full_price.py` replay: builder, `validateBoundManifest` and `verifyClaim` (against a real README) all pass. Fix: bind the command to the claim's own package path or to a per-claim line.

**Q1-6 [important; 2 reads] AMEND rows are bound by position.** `museum_data.py:430-450` zips `open_specs` with the three rows with no content check (unlike the bullet checks at `:401-404`); `museum.mjs:65` id by slot, `:79` D5 proof = `index_source`, `:84-85` D5 pointer checked against the PROOF_INDEX line, not the row. Probe `substitution/p6_open_row_position.{py,mjs}`: a successor STATUS (labelled HYPOTHETICAL) with a different obligation in slot 2 and re-pinned sources yields id `d5-pin-neighborhoods-open` with the new title and reason but the D5 pin-neighborhood review link and "NO COMPLETE PROOF YET"; builder and guard accept and render it. Fix: bind each open spec to its row's title or id.

**Q1-7 [minor; 2 reads]** Shipped D1 AMEND card says "Review pointer in the verified index" and "Open review", but its pointer source is `STATUS.md` and the target is what the STATUS row calls the "fail-closed reopening" (`museum.mjs:151, 83`; `museum_data.py:444`). Probe `substitution/p7_labels.mjs`.

**Q1-8 [minor; 2 reads]** The shipped D5 height-window card's "Open source illustration" leads to the annulus exhibit, whose pinned source is the *all-height* proof (`rn_annulus_bridge_20260925/PROOF.md`, blob `6f317515`), titled for that other claim; the builder's `scope_boundary` sentence for it is never rendered (`museum.mjs:6-7`; `museum_data.py:509-510`). Probe `substitution/p7_labels.mjs`.

**Q1-9 [minor; 2 reads]** `claims/LANDING_CLAIMS.json@d6628da` is pinned and byte-verified (`museum_data.py:122-129`) but never read; for the same proof blobs it records D2 `FAIL_CLOSED` and D3/D4 `HOLD_WITH_DOMAIN` while the cards show the builder constant "Source label: ACCEPT" (`:423-426`). STATUS and PROOF_INDEX do support ACCEPT at the stated scopes; the finding is that a pinned source's conflicting machine-readable axis is dropped silently. Probe `substitution/p8_landing_axis.py`.

**Q2 — mutable review-comment pointers vs immutable pointer-source identities**

**Q2-F1 [critical; 2 reads, both critical] A "Byte-verified review" card's "Open review" link can point to any URL.** `museum.mjs:40` validates `review_url` only when `pointer_only===true`; `:86` binds a non-pointer review by path only; `:151` renders `anchor('Open review ↗', review.review_url||review.html_url)`. Probe `pointers/p1_review_url_on_byte_verified_review.mjs` + `ci_sim.py`: a correct digest-verified identity plus `review_url: https://example.invalid/forged-review` (also an issue comment, also a `blob/main` URL) passes `validateDescriptor`, `validateBoundManifest`, the generator, the 12 Python tests, `museum_check` (15/15 including the actual-pinned-museum integration test) and the geometry tests; the card says "Byte-verified review", shows the pinned sha256 under "Review source identity", and its click target is the forged URL; `pointer_only:true` with the same URL is refused. A hand edit of `museum.json` is caught by `check_export`; a generator edit is not. Fix: refuse `review_url` unless `pointer_only===true`; render non-pointer anchors from `html_url` only.

**Q2-F2 [important; 2 reads] Pointers bound by substring: any prefix of a quoted URL passes; the generator binds no AMEND-row pointer at all.** `museum.mjs:85`; `museum_data.py:401-406` (any link target in the bullet, e.g. D2's bare `main #67` "remains open" link) and `:430-446` (nothing for the three AMEND rows). Probe `pointers/p2_pointer_substring_binding.mjs`, `p2b_python_any_link_target.py`, `ci_sim.py F2_d1_pointer_prefix`: `…/issues/6`, `…/issues/7`, `#issuecomment-584` pass; an edited D1 target of `…/issues/6` regenerates and passes the whole museum CI, displayed as "Review pointer in the verified index" over the genuine pointer-source digest. Fix: exact link-target equality on both sides; bind AMEND-row pointers to their row.

**Q2-F3 [important; 2 reads] The only on-card statement that a review is a mutable comment is free text.** `review_notice` is checked only for non-emptiness (`museum.mjs:40`) and no test pins it. Probe `pointers/ci_sim.py F3_notice_claims_byte_frozen`: notice rewritten in the generator to "Byte-frozen review: the linked comment is sealed by the SHA-256 shown below." regenerates and passes every museum CI step; the D2 ACCEPT-scoped card then tells readers a mutable comment is sealed by the PROOF_INDEX digest. Fix: fixed literal per class in `museum.mjs`, or exact-equality allow-list, plus a rendered-text test.

**Q2-F4 [important; 2 reads] A byte-verified review is bound by path suffix only; a mutable `blob/main` link satisfies it.** `museum.mjs:51-53, 86`. Probe `pointers/p3_byte_verified_review_identity_unbound.mjs` (+ `p6_controls.mjs`): (a) d5-pin with `pointer_only` removed: the STATUS row's `…/Math-/blob/main/PROOF_INDEX.md)` matches the `/PROOF_INDEX.md)` clause, so the card flips from "Review pointer" to "Byte-verified review" (refused on the other five pointer cards: control); (b) the same review path at Math-@`bebb77ae` or `query-@ffff…` passes; (c) a file named just `REVIEW.md` in any allow-listed repository, at any commit, is "contained" in every quote that links some `…/REVIEW.md`, so forged bytes with a self-consistent digest at that identity pass. Fix: as Q1-2 plus exact-target matching.

**Q2-F5 [minor; finder said important, both second readers minor; 2 reads] Every comment-pointer card's strip says "Review wording is quoted at its declared scope" although no review wording is quoted or bound.** `museum.mjs:160` (strip on every card), `:114` (the "review" step of a pointer re-verifies PROOF_INDEX/STATUS bytes, not the comment). Probe `pointers/p4_comment_edit_invisible.mjs`: serving an "ACCEPT WITHDRAWN" edit at every review URL changes nothing (0 requests to github.com; rendered cards byte-identical). The per-card "not byte-frozen" notice partly mitigates; the pinned index's own date ("checked on 2026-09-26") is not shown. Fix: a pointer-specific strip text and the index date.

**Q2-F6 [minor; 2 reads]** Shipped-card label defects: the D1 pointer source is STATUS, not "the verified index"; D2/D3/D4 source lines cite two review comments jointly but the single "Open review" goes to one chosen by a hard-coded spec (D2: the R5/R6 delta only); D1's "Open review" is the reopening; the d5-pin pointer is bound to a PROOF_INDEX line the card never displays. Probe `pointers/p5_pointer_labels_and_selection.mjs`.

**Q3 — packet membership at the declared snapshot**

**Q3-F1 [important; 2 reads] Nothing checks that a source is in the tree of its declared commit: `read_source` falls back to the working tree, and the harness serves those bytes under the pinned-commit URL.** `tools/museum_data.py:466-475` (`git show <commit>:<path>`, on any failure `read_bytes()` from the root); `museum_check.py` builds `MUSEUM_FIXTURE` keyed by URL, so the node test cannot tell. Probes `membership/p1_fallback_unit.py`, `p1_ci_false_green.sh` (all outputs in `ALL_OUTPUT.txt`): with the main pin moved to `bd9fc9d6` (a real main commit whose tree has no `incoming/`), or to a side-branch commit, or to a nonexistent commit, `read_source` accepts the working-tree bytes, the generator emits the packet "at" that commit, and `museum_check` passes 15/15 and exits 0; a strict `commit:path` read refuses all three. In CI (`fetch-depth: 0`) the fallback fires only for a path absent at the commit, an unknown commit, or a shallow/sparse checkout. The live page fails closed (raw-at-commit 404 → refusal card); the defect is in the generator and the CI gate. Fix: refuse when `git show` fails for a (commit, path) the manifest declares; never fall back silently.

**Q3-F2 [minor; 2 reads]** The packet list is hard-coded and never compared with `incoming/` at the declared commit; `MAIN_COMMIT` is unused; the summary prints a fixed count. Probes `membership/p2_omission.sh`, `p2c_empty_list_ci.sh`: with the main pin moved to `a12c178c` (the real merge of #150, two packets in tree, STATUS/SARD/notebook byte-identical to the pins), generator, `museum_check` (15/15) and a strict render all say verified while showing one packet. Omitting the packet entirely is caught (`museum_check` requires the packet card). Fix: list `incoming/` at the commit and compare.

**Q3-F3 [minor; single-reader]** Nothing checks that the declared snapshot is on the default branch. Probe `membership/p3_unlanded_snapshot.sh`: the main pin moved to `3b8c4545` ("TEST ONLY … NEVER MERGE", on `origin/chatgpt/never-merge-formal-negative-20260927`, not an ancestor of main or of `d77a85a7`) passes generator, `museum_check` (15/15) and a strict raw-at-commit render, while the page says "These are pinned landed submissions"; zero ancestry/default-branch checks in the three files. Fix: assert `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> origin/main` in the generator.

**Q3-F4 [minor; single-reader]** The unit tests read STATUS.md from the live working tree, not the snapshot: one unrelated appended line breaks 6 tests, including `test_historical_snapshot_ignores_unrelated_working_tree_append`, and makes a negative control fail for the wrong reason (`source identity mismatch` instead of `review pointer`). Probe `membership/p4_status_moving_ref.sh`. Current main reads a fixture file instead, which fixes this there.

**Q3-F5 [minor; single-reader]** `test_historical_snapshot_ignores_unrelated_working_tree_append` (`tests/test_museum_data.py:112-133`) is not isolated from an inherited `GIT_DIR`: it runs `git init`, `add` and `commit` against whatever repository `GIT_DIR` names, then passes. Probe `membership/p5_test_writes_inherited_gitdir.sh` (re-run tonight into an isolated throwaway repository: one commit "Pin historical status fixture" by `Museum Test Fixture`, 56 insertions). See §5. Fix: run the test's git commands with an explicit `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` for the temporary directory and `env -u GIT_DIR`.

**Q4 — response size and time limits**

**Q4-1 [minor; single-reader]** `boundedFetch` returns early on a non-OK response without aborting the controller or cancelling the body (`museum.mjs:22`); `verifiedBytes` then refuses it, so this is resource hygiene, fails closed. Probe `limits/p1_nonok_body_not_released.mjs`: 404/500/503 → `signal.aborted=false body.cancelled=false`; over-cap 200 → aborted and cancelled.

**Q4-2 [minor; single-reader]** The size and time bound lives in `startMuseum`'s private `cachedFetch`; the exported `verifyClaim(claim, fetcher=fetch)` reaches `core.mjs` `verifiedBytes`, which buffers the whole body with no signal or cap (`museum.mjs:111-119`; `core.mjs:22-24`); the module's own integration test calls it with a raw fetcher. Probe `limits/p2_verifyclaim_default_unbounded.mjs`: default fetcher refuses a 64 MiB body only after buffering it (pin 13 B); a stalled body is still pending at 25 s; `boundedFetch` contrast refuses after 4 MiB. Production at `cd32303` is bounded. Fix: cap `verifiedBytes` at `pin.bytes` with a deadline.

**Q4-3 [minor; single-reader]** No negative control pins `startMuseum`'s use of `boundedFetch`. Probe `limits/p6_bound_wiring_mutants.mjs`: four mutants (manifest fetch unbounded; `cachedFetch` bypasses `boundedFetch`; both; defaults raised to 1 GiB / 1 day) all pass 14/14 of `test_museum_frontend.mjs` (pinned test skipped offline; by inspection its fetcher returns complete in-memory responses ≤ 61,961 B and cannot detect them either).

**Q4-4 [minor; single-reader]** CI checks the 256 KiB `museum.json` cap against `JSON.stringify(manifest)` (`tests/test_museum_frontend.mjs:134`), about 11% smaller than the pretty-printed bytes `museum_data.dump()` writes; nothing bounds the export at build time. Probe `limits/p3_manifest_cap_tested_on_reserialized_bytes.mjs`: an export padded to exactly the cap in compact form passes the CI path and is refused by the production path ("Response exceeds byte limit"). Fails closed; current headroom 4.64×.

**Q4-5 [minor; single-reader]** `read_source`'s `urlopen(..., timeout=30)` is a per-socket-operation timeout, not a deadline (`museum_data.py:477-478`). Probe `limits/p4_urlopen_timeout_is_per_recv.py` (stdlib `HTTPResponse.read` over a local socketpair, last two bytes 20 s apart): accepted after 40.0 s with no error; one byte per 29.9 s would allow 21.4 days for the largest pin. CI's 5-minute job timeout turns this into a failure; local runs have no bound. Bytes are still hash-verified.

**Q4-6 [minor; single-reader]** The local read paths read the whole `git show` output or working-tree file before any size check, following symlinks (`museum_data.py:466-475`), unlike the network path's `read(bytes+1)`. Probe `limits/p5_local_fallback_uncapped.py` (child processes, 1 GiB RLIMIT_AS, 10 s): a FIFO at a pinned path blocks indefinitely; a `/dev/zero` symlink raises `MemoryError`; a 300 MiB file is read fully before the mismatch error. Not reached in CI at `cd32303`. Fix: regular files only, read at most `bytes+1`, give `git show` a timeout.

**Q4-7 [minor; single-reader]** The geometry import and `mountGeometry` are the only unbounded awaits in `startMuseum` (`museum.mjs:176, 202, 206`). Probe `limits/p8_geometry_loader_no_deadline.mjs`: a stalled loader leaves `museum-state` at the interim text indefinitely with all 14 cards rendered; a rejecting loader produces an honest refusal. The interim text claims nothing, so this is consistency only.

**Fail-open sweep (no question asked for it; added because fail-open is the museum's property)**

**FO-1 [critical; single-reader] Status-bearing card text (`proof.availability`, `replay.notice`, `replay.url` without `replay.source`) is never bound to a source.** `museum.mjs:79` (`sameIdentity` compares eight keys, not availability), `:96-98` (notice non-empty only; url shape only; nothing fetched without a source), `:146-148, 156-158` (rendered as given); `museum_data.py:440-449` (generator literals that no test pins). Probes `failopen/p1_availability_unbound.mjs`, `p5_replay_unbound.mjs`, `p6_generator_path_ci_green.py`: with `availability` deleted on the two open obligations, the link reads "Open pinned full proof" instead of "Open pinned source contract" and both "NO COMPLETE PROOF YET" and "No landed proof is supplied for this open obligation." disappear, `validateBoundManifest` passes and the banner says verified; arbitrary availability text is printed verbatim; an AMEND card accepts "Replay reproduces the closed parent theorem. ACCEPT." plus an unverified `replay.url` (0 requests). A generator edit to these literals regenerates and passes every museum CI step. Mitigation: class AMEND/open is enforced, so "OPEN / NOT LANDED" stays and the card contradicts itself rather than flipping class. Fix: derive these strings from class and id in `museum.mjs`, or exact-equality allow-list per id, with negative controls. Validation-only re-probe: persists on current main (§7).

**FO-2 [important; single-reader]** `pointer_only` type confusion: the guard at `:40` runs for `=== true`, the binding at `:82-85` and the renderer at `:151-154` branch on truthiness, and `includes('')` is vacuously true. Probe `failopen/p2_pointer_only_truthy.mjs`: `pointer_only:1, review_url:""` passes (the byte-frozen sard-g review can be replaced by a pseudo-pointer to the index; the not-byte-frozen notice is dropped); `pointer_only:true` with the same input is refused. Mutant M13 (delete the line-40 guard) survives S1–S4. Reaching it needs a manifest that differs from the generator output, which `museum_check` catches in CI; the browser validator does not. Fix: `typeof pointer_only === 'boolean'`, `=== true` everywhere, non-empty `review_url` equal to one exact link target.

**FO-3 [important; single-reader] The live page's verification wiring has no negative control.** Every substitution control calls `validateBoundManifest` or `verifyClaim` directly; the only `startMuseum` assertions on pinned data are the banner text and `claim-cards.children.length === 14` (`tests/test_museum_frontend.mjs:142-143`), which counts placeholder hosts that exist whether a card rendered or was refused. Probe `failopen/mutants.py` + `p3_mutant_impact.py` + `p7_banner_and_count.mjs`: mutants M31 (never call `validateBoundManifest`), M32 (index/status bytes used without digest check), M33 (cards without `verifyClaim`), M21 (claim catch renders as verified), M20 (banner always verified), M22, M23, M16 all survive S1–S4; under M31 an AMEND row promoted to ACCEPT-scoped renders fully verified, under M21 a proof with a wrong digest does. Fix: `startMuseum`-level controls feeding tampered manifests and bytes, asserting the refusal card and the absent `data-object-id`; count rendered vs refused cards.

**FO-4 [important; single-reader] Most individual `validateBoundManifest` guards can be deleted with CI green**, including the cross-claim review-substitution guard named in the offer. Probe `failopen/mutants.py`: M01 title, M02 byte-frozen review-file binding, M03 AMEND reason, M04–M06 replay declaration/URL/checkout, M07 packet cap, M08 proof repo/commit = index, M09 D1 parent, M10 open-claim identity, M12 D5 open-review pin, M13, M14 id order, M15 row counts, M18 RESULT.md declarations, M19 exhibit quote, M25–M27 (drop "source contract" label, "OPEN / NOT LANDED", the not-byte-frozen notice) all survive S1–S4. Under M02 the D6 P15 review renders as the "Byte-verified review" of the D5 all-height annulus with the banner verified; the original refuses it ("Review file differs from the source quote"). The integration test substitutes only the proof (claims[3]←[10]), `status_quote` and the replay command, never the review. Fix: one negative control per guard, asserting its specific error.

**FO-5 [minor; single-reader]** `museum_data.project()` (`:408-409`) defaults a missing STATUS ACCEPT row to `status_quote None` and takes the first of duplicate rows, then prints "Museum projection verified"; the browser requires exactly one row (`museum.mjs:90-94`) and refuses, so only the Python step fails open. Probe `failopen/p4_status_quote_default.py`. Fix: mirror the browser rule in `project()`.
